{"summary":"Main result: H9.1's premise is wrong. In both hiverge and Fable e1, the "target magnitude" that decays from 0.5012 to 0.0786 scales the gradient matrix just before Newton-Schulz. The next line renormalizes X/||X||_F, so the scaling cancels and is dead code. Their real weight renorm uses a constant target of sqrt(len(p)) (the out-channel count). E082 therefore tested a mechanism neither recipe has: a 6x effective-LR increase. Retire H9.1 and H9.1.1 instead of building a "decay target plus LR" follow-up.

Second, the tree misdescribes how the reference recipes treat the whitening bias. hiverge and Fable train it for 0.2 of an epoch (ceil(0.2*len(train_loader)), about 7 steps at bs 1536, ~3% of steps), not for 20% of steps. They then cut it off with b.detach() inside forward, keyed on a bool. Airbench94 trains it for 3 epochs and then disables its gradient "to increase backward-pass throughput ... without reducing accuracy" (no number given). This supports H2.15's mechanism. It also means a freeze at about 0.2 epoch is the recipes' own setting, not an extrapolation. E061 only zeroed the LR, which saves no backward compute.

Third, Fable's tail is not "an EMA over the last ~8 steps". With train_epochs 8.875, decay_epochs 8.5 and ema_start = decay_steps − 8, the EMA starts 8 steps before the floor is reached and runs through the whole ~12-step floor-hold. That is a window of about 20 steps (~5 lerps at 0.3). E081 (a 20-step window, refuted) was therefore close to Fable's actual design. The tip's ~8-step window is its own variant, and E081/E083 suggest it suits this regime better.

Smaller items:
- NorMuon gave no gain on CIFAR-10 airbench (93.82 vs 93.90 for Muon(N)). A per-row-normalized Muon is a low-prior structural candidate.
- FrozenBN in the late phase would remove BN reductions in the 32 px tail, but Wu & Johnson find it underperforms regular BN at large normalization batches. It is speculative, with a low prior.

structured_output.summary:
Main result: H9.1's premise is wrong. In both hiverge and Fable e1, the "target magnitude" that decays from 0.5012 to 0.0786 scales the gradient matrix just before Newton-Schulz. The next line renormalizes X/||X||_F, so the scaling cancels and is dead code. Their real weight renorm uses a constant target of sqrt(len(p)) (the out-channel count). E082 therefore tested a mechanism neither recipe has: a 6x effective-LR increase. Retire H9.1 and H9.1.1 instead of building a "decay target plus LR" follow-up.

Second, the tree misdescribes how the reference recipes treat the whitening bias. hiverge and Fable train it for 0.2 of an epoch (ceil(0.2*len(train_loader)), about 7 steps at bs 1536, ~3% of steps), not for 20% of steps. They then cut it off with b.detach() inside forward, keyed on a bool. Airbench94 trains it for 3 epochs and then disables its gradient "to increase backward-pass throughput ... without reducing accuracy" (no number given). This supports H2.15's mechanism. It also means a freeze at about 0.2 epoch is the recipes' own setting, not an extrapolation. E061 only zeroed the LR, which saves no backward compute.

Third, Fable's tail is not "an EMA over the last ~8 steps". With train_epochs 8.875, decay_epochs 8.5 and ema_start = decay_steps − 8, the EMA starts 8 steps before the floor is reached and runs through the whole ~12-step floor-hold. That is a window of about 20 steps (~5 lerps at 0.3). E081 (a 20-step window, refuted) was therefore close to Fable's actual design. The tip's ~8-step window is its own variant, and E081/E083 suggest it suits this regime better.

Smaller items:
- NorMuon gave no gain on CIFAR-10 airbench (93.82 vs 93.90 for Muon(N)). A per-row-normalized Muon is a low-prior structural candidate.
- FrozenBN in the late phase would remove BN reductions in the 32 px tail, but Wu & Johnson find it underperforms regular BN at large normalization batches. It is speculative, with a low prior.
- No public CIFAR-100 leaderboard entries were found beyond the futurebiohackers 8.11 s / 75.29% SGD recipe. The AIDDA repo has no PRs, and its baseline is ResNet9 at 59.3 s.
- Fable's write-up quantifies only progressive resizing. It also reports that a 60 s untimed GPU cooldown was worth ~0.04 s, which is specification gaming (sleeps are banned here). That confirms the thermal/energy-bound sensitivity.

findings.claim: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, target_magnitude = 0.5012*(1-p) + 0.0786*p is applied as X = X * target_magnitude/(||X||+1e-5). The very next lines are X_norm = X.norm(dim=(1,2)); X = X/(X_norm+1e-5), followed by 3 quintic NS steps (a,b,c = 3.4576, -4.7391, 2.0843). The magnitude schedule therefore cancels and is a no-op. The separate weight renorm (every norm_freq = 2+int(15*progress) steps) multiplies each filter by len(p.data)**0.5/||p||, a constant target of sqrt(out_channels). The Muon lr (0.205) decays linearly to 0 with the other non-whitening groups.
findings.relevance: H9.1 rests on 'hiverge and Fable decay the renorm target from 0.5012 to 0.0786', and E082 implemented a weight-norm target decay that collapsed training. Neither reference recipe has that mechanism, so the premise is false, not merely mis-tuned.

findings.claim: Fable e1's _ns_one does the same thing: X = X*(tm/(mags+1e-5)) and then X = X/(X.norm(dim=(1,2))+1e-5) before 3 NS iterations, so tm is dead code here too. The whitening-bias forward is F.conv2d(x, self.whiten.weight, b if whiten_bias_grad else b.detach()), so the bias is detached (not just given LR 0) after whiten_bias_epochs = 0.2. The whitening weight has requires_grad=False, and BN weights have requires_grad=False.
findings.relevance: This confirms Fable uses a real detach-based freeze, which makes H2.15's backward-skip possible. The tree's note that 'Fable e1 only zeroes the LR' is wrong: Fable does both (LR schedule plus detach). It also confirms again that the renorm-target premise of H9.1 is void.

findings.claim: whiten_bias_train_steps = ceil(0.2 * len(train_loader)), i.e. 0.2 epoch (~7 steps at bs 1536), not 20% of total steps. During those steps the whitening-bias LR decays linearly to zero (lr_factor1 = 1 - step/whiten_bias_train_steps), and after them the bias is detached. hiverge also has no LR warmup, LS 0.09, total 7.65 epochs, Muon momentum 0.655, and SGD momentum 0.825 for the whitening bias, norm biases and head.
findings.relevance: The tree states that 'hiverge and Fable train the whitening bias only for the first 20% of steps' (H8.1, H2.15). The actual setting is ~0.2 epoch, about 3% of steps. A freeze at 0.2 epoch is therefore the references' standard configuration, so H2.15.1 could freeze much earlier than E061's point, with more 16/24/32 px steps getting the backward saving. The accuracy risk is untested on CIFAR-100, where the tip trains this bias at 64x LR.

findings.claim: Airbench paper: the whitening-layer biases 'are trained for 3 epochs, after which we disable their gradient to increase backward-pass throughput, which improves training speed without reducing accuracy.' The paper gives no separate speed number. BN affine scale parameters are disabled.
findings.relevance: This is primary-source support that disabling gradient flow into the stem is a throughput lever with no accuracy cost on CIFAR-10. It backs H2.15's mechanism, although the size of the saving must still be measured (the tree estimates 1-2.5%).

findings.claim: Fable hyperparameters: train_epochs 8.875, decay_epochs 8.5, lr_floor 0.05, ema_start_before 8, ema_every 4, ema_decay 0.7 (foreach_lerp with weight 0.3), batch_size 1536, res_schedule [24,24,24,28,28,28,32,32,32], LS 0.09, ortho_lr 0.2255, ortho_momentum 0.655. ema_start = decay_steps - 8, so the final EMA starts 8 steps before the LR reaches its floor and continues through the whole floor-hold (0.375 epoch, ~12 steps), a window of ~20 steps and ~5 updates.
findings.relevance: The tree describes Fable's tail as a 'light final EMA over the last ~8 steps'. Fable's real window spans pre-floor iterates plus the full floor-hold, which is what E081 tested (refuted on this tip). The tip's 8-step, post-floor-only window is a local variant that appears better here. This helps interpret H6.5 and H6.5.3: the averaging design is already locally tuned and closed, consistent with E081 and E083.

findings.claim: Fable's counted 7.6% gain is attributed mainly to progressive resizing. Pooling, CUDA-graph and optimizer-fusion work are not individually quantified. Excluded specification gaming included a 60-second untimed GPU cooldown worth ~0.04 s per run and machine selection worth ~0.009 s.
findings.relevance: There is no external quantification of the systems levers, so H2.14 and H2.15 sizes must come from local measurements. The cooldown effect shows that thermal and energy state measurably affects time on these energy-bound runs. That is consistent with H2.4 and the trial-to-trial time noise in H4, but it is not a usable lever because sleeps are banned.

findings.claim: CIFARNET (2M params, CIFAR-10 airbench-style), mean ± SE over 5 seeds: Muon(N) 93.90±0.08, NorMuon(N) 93.82±0.05, NorMuon(H) 94.05±0.09, NorMuonT(H) 93.96±0.09, SGDM 92.36, AdamW 92.44.
findings.relevance: Row-wise (neuron-wise) normalized Muon variants give at most ~+0.15 pp over Muon on an airbench-style CNN, within ~1-2 SE. If NorMuon is considered as a structural Muon change under H9/H7, its prior should be low.

findings.claim: On a CIFAR-10 airbench CNN, Muon variants (full vs randomized/inexact polar decomposition) reach essentially the same test accuracy, with indistinguishable convergence curves. All beat AdamW and SGD-Nesterov.
findings.relevance: This is weak external support that the exact form of the orthogonalizer is not an accuracy lever in this regime. It is consistent with the tree closing the cheaper-orthogonalizer line (H7.2), together with E031's finding that NS iteration count matters.

findings.claim: Wu & Johnson: replacing BN with FrozenBN (fixed population statistics) for the last 20 of 100 ImageNet epochs nearly matches regular BN when the normalization batch is tiny. But 'tuning with FrozenBN underperforms regular BN' when the normalization batch is already large enough. EMA statistics 'often fall out of the distribution of mini-batch statistics', especially early.
findings.relevance: This bears on a new, untried time lever: switching to FrozenBN or population statistics in the final part of the energy-bound 32 px phase, which removes BN's per-channel reductions in forward and backward (elementwise is ~29-31% of GPU time, E067). The evidence says it costs accuracy at large batch (bs 1536 here), so the prior is low. If tried at all, limit it to the floor-hold steps and measure the saving untimed first.

findings.claim: The benchmark repo has no public PRs or leaderboard entries. The only reference is a ResNet9 baseline at 75.36% / 59.30 s (A100 80GB PCIe, 2 trials). The only public competing recipe found is futurebiohackers PR #3: SGD airbench-style, 75.29% in 8.11 s on A100-SXM4, where Muon 'lost every comparison' and was dropped.
findings.relevance: No external CIFAR-100 recipe beats the tip (~4.58 s). The futurebiohackers negative Muon result was already overturned locally (E019). No new external lever comes from competitors.
